method: open-Li get_element_profile(Li, SE); decomposition at each anode reservoir V (Li metal 0 V, Li-In ~0.62 V). leaky = MP gap < 2.0 eV (electron-conducting interphase). MP GGA/GGA+U.

0.00.reaction: Li58B2P8S41Cl16O3 -> 2 LiB + 3 Li2O + 8 Li3P + 16 LiCl + 41 S + 10 Li

interpretation: vs BARE Li METAL (0 V): b2o3 is WORSE than undoped -- the B dopant forms METALLIC LiB (gap 0) -> min gap 0.0 vs undoped 0.7 (Li3P). BUT vs Li-In (~0.62 V, the standard sulfide-ASSB lab anode): the metallic LiB does NOT form (B -> B6P + Li3BO3) -> b2o3 min gap 0.7 (Li3P only), same leaky tier as undoped-at-Li-metal; undoped at Li-In is even milder (1.89, P2S7, no Li3P). => b2o3's worst anode liability (metallic LiB) is specific to bare Li metal and is AVOIDED with a Li-In anode -> practically manageable (which is why sulfide ASSBs use Li-In). Thermodynamic products only; morphology/kinetics not modeled.
